crew.overview: Recently fired and desperate for work, a troubled young man named Mike agrees to take a position as a night security guard at an abandoned theme restaurant: Freddy Fazbear's Pizzeria. But he soon discovers that nothing at Freddy's is what it seems.
crew.title: Five Nights at Freddy's

crew.overview: Finney Blake, a shy but clever 13-year-old boy, is abducted by a sadistic killer and trapped in a soundproof basement where screaming is of little use. When a disconnected phone on the wall begins to ring, Finney discovers that he can hear the voices of the killer’s previous victims. And they are dead set on making sure that what happened to them doesn’t happen to Finney.
crew.title: The Black Phone

crew.overview: Seventeen-year-old Stella spends most of her time in the hospital as a cystic fibrosis patient. Her life is full of routines, boundaries and self-control — all of which get put to the test when she meets Will, an impossibly charming teen who has the same illness. There's an instant flirtation, though restrictions dictate that they must maintain a safe distance between them. As their connection intensifies, so does the temptation to throw the rules out the window and embrace that attraction.

details.biography: Christopher H. Warner’s career began in production for scripted television where he quickly climbed the ranks working on numerous projects including “Gilmore Girls”, “CSI: NY” and “Nip/Tuck”. He soon shifted his talents to feature films, starting with the 2005 Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie blockbuster, Mr. & Mrs. Smith, then later serving as Production Supervisor on the Official 2012 Cannes Film Festival selection, Mud directed by Jeff Nichols and starring Matthew McConaughey and Damien Chazelle’s Academy-award® winning Whiplash starring Miles Teller. In 2015, Warner made a return to television as a Production Manager for Netflix’s critically acclaimed series “Narcos”.
details.name: Christopher H. Warner
